correctness.rationale: A direct proof turns Haar two-point geodesic distance on any flat 3-torus into the radial volume of its Voronoi cell. Every facet midpoint is relatively interior by central symmetry of the shared Voronoi facet. Differentiating sphere area gives the union of forbidden spherical caps. Individual newborn caps add the exact derivative 2π/r each, disjointly, while exposed arcs of old circles vary continuously by dominated convergence across all tangencies and intersections. Thus only facet radii cause jumps, each of size -2πr/V. Volume is independently recovered from the small-ball law. Orthogonal-box exact formulas and Sobol numerical checks ran successfully; finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement concerns the exact negative second-derivative jump spectrum of the Haar-geodesic distance CDF on every Euclidean flat 3-torus. The key additional result is the no-false-jumps property under arbitrary simultaneous facet/edge/vertex critical radii, yielding the full Voronoi-relevant norm multiset; the planar square-root law does not imply it and classical Voronoi facet correspondences do not study distance histograms. Examined primary Voronoi full text and distance-histogram summaries provide no stronger covering statement. Priority is provisional due to incomplete access to a relevant broad later inverse-distribution paper.

value.rationale: A natural one-dimensional observable (the full distribution of geodesic distances of two Haar points) recovers a nontrivial geometric length multiset and the number of Voronoi facets for arbitrary three-dimensional flat tori. The absence of false jumps at simultaneous face/edge/vertex critical radii is essential: without it, the distance statistic would not yield a reliable invariant. The result is not a special-box tabulation, genericity restriction, or full-isometry claim.
